title: Time: Clocks, a.m. and p.m., and the Calendar
seo_title: Time – Primary 4 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Tell time on analogue and digital clocks; use a.m. and p.m.; convert between hours, minutes and seconds; use the calendar (days, weeks, months and years). (summary of the NERDC Primary 4 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 4 maths worksheets on time: hours, minutes and seconds, a.m. and p.m., time taken, the calendar and time word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: a.m. before noon, p.m. after noon.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • 1 minute = 60 seconds, 1 hour = 60 minutes, 1 day = 24 hours, 1 week = 7 days, 1 year = 12 months.
  • a.m. is from midnight to midday (morning); p.m. is from midday to midnight.
  • To find time taken, count on: first to the next hour, then the rest.

Examples

Example

8:45 a.m. to 11:20 a.m.

8:45 → 9:00 = 15 min

9:00 → 11:20 = 2 h 20 min

Answer: 2 hours 35 minutes

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Treating time like decimals1 hour 30 minutes is not 1.30 hours.
Mixing up a.m. and p.m.School starts in the morning (a.m.).
Forgetting months have different lengths30 days hath September, April, June and November.

faq.q: How many days are in a leap year?

items.q: Convert. 48 hours = ☐ days
items.e: 24 hours = 1 day, so 48 ÷ 24 = 2 days.

items.q: Convert. 140 days = ☐ weeks
items.e: 7 days = 1 week, so 140 ÷ 7 = 20 weeks.

items.q: Convert. 2 days = ☐ hours
items.e: 1 day = 24 hours, so 2 × 24 = 48 hours.

items.q: Convert. 13 weeks = ☐ days
items.e: 1 week = 7 days, so 13 × 7 = 91 days.

items.q: Convert. 11 hours = ☐ minutes
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes, so 11 × 60 = 660 minutes.

items.q: Convert. 11 days = ☐ hours
items.e: 1 day = 24 hours, so 11 × 24 = 264 hours.

items.q: Convert. 660 seconds = ☐ minutes
items.e: 60 seconds = 1 minute, so 660 ÷ 60 = 11 minutes.

items.q: Convert. 168 hours = ☐ days
items.e: 24 hours = 1 day, so 168 ÷ 24 = 7 days.

items.q: Convert. 2 minutes = ☐ seconds
items.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds, so 2 × 60 = 120 seconds.

items.q: Convert. 84 days = ☐ weeks
items.e: 7 days = 1 week, so 84 ÷ 7 = 12 weeks.

items.q: Convert. 3 hours = ☐ minutes
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes (not 100). Multiply: 3 × 60 = 180, so 3 hours = 180 minutes.

items.q: Convert. 4 minutes = ☐ seconds
items.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds. Multiply: 4 × 60 = 240, so 4 minutes = 240 seconds.

items.q: Convert. 9 minutes = ☐ seconds
items.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds. Multiply: 9 × 60 = 540, so 9 minutes = 540 seconds.

items.q: Convert. 300 seconds = ☐ minutes
items.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds. Seconds to minutes: divide. 300 ÷ 60 = 5, because 5 × 60 = 300.

items.q: Convert. 240 minutes = ☐ hours
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. Minutes to hours: divide. 240 ÷ 60 = 4, because 4 × 60 = 240. 2 hours 40 minutes would mean 1 hour = 100 minutes.

items.q: Convert. 3 years = ☐ months
items.e: 1 year = 12 months. Multiply: 3 × 12 = 36, so 3 years = 36 months.

items.q: Convert. 60 months = ☐ years
items.e: 1 year = 12 months. Months to years: divide. 60 ÷ 12 = 5, because 5 × 12 = 60.

items.q: Convert. 5 weeks = ☐ days
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. Multiply: 5 × 7 = 35, so 5 weeks = 35 days.

items.q: Convert. 28 days = ☐ weeks
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. Days to weeks: divide. 28 ÷ 7 = 4, so 28 days = 4 weeks.

items.q: Convert. 2 days = ☐ hours
items.e: 1 day = 24 hours. Multiply: 2 × 24 = 48, so 2 days = 48 hours.

items.q: How much time passes from 9:15 to 9:35?
items.e: Count on from 9:15 to 9:35: 35 − 15 = 20 minutes.

items.q: How much time passes from 9:05 to 9:50?
items.e: Count on from 9:05 to 9:50: 50 − 5 = 45 minutes.

items.q: How much time passes from 2:00 to 2:15?
items.e: Count on from 2:00 to 2:15: 15 − 0 = 15 minutes.

items.q: How much time passes from 3:30 to 3:55?
items.e: Count on from 3:30 to 3:55: 55 − 30 = 25 minutes.

items.q: How much time passes from 7:25 to 7:45?

items.q: How much time passes from 3:05 to 3:35?
items.e: Count on from 3:05 to 3:35: 35 − 5 = 30 minutes.

items.q: How much time passes from 9:21 to 10:20?
items.e: Jump to the next hour first: 9:21 to 10:00 is 39 minutes. Then 10:00 to 10:20 is 20 minutes. 39 + 20 = 59 minutes.

items.q: How much time passes from 8:45 to 9:25?
items.e: Jump to the next hour first: 8:45 to 9:00 is 15 minutes. Then 9:00 to 9:25 is 25 minutes. 15 + 25 = 40 minutes.

items.q: How much time passes from 7:30 to 8:25?

items.q: How much time passes from 6:54 to 7:49?

items.q: How much time passes from 7:40 to 8:28?
items.e: Jump to the next hour first: 7:40 to 8:00 is 20 minutes. Then 8:00 to 8:28 is 28 minutes. 20 + 28 = 48 minutes.

items.q: How much time passes from 5:27 to 6:12?
items.e: Jump to the next hour first: 5:27 to 6:00 is 33 minutes. Then 6:00 to 6:12 is 12 minutes. 33 + 12 = 45 minutes.

items.q: How much time passes from 4:50 to 5:14?

items.q: How much time passes from 3:00 to 4:45?
items.e: From 3:00 to 4:45 is 1 hour 45 minutes.

items.q: How much time passes from 6:50 to 8:00?
items.e: Jump to the next hour first: 6:50 to 7:00 is 10 minutes. Then 7:00 to 8:00 is 60 minutes. 10 + 60 = 1 hour 10 minutes.

items.q: How much time passes from 2:35 to 4:05?
items.e: Jump to the next hour first: 2:35 to 3:00 is 25 minutes. Then 3:00 to 4:05 is 65 minutes. 25 + 65 = 1 hour 30 minutes.

items.q: How much time passes from 5:25 to 6:30?
items.e: Jump to the next hour first: 5:25 to 6:00 is 35 minutes. Then 6:00 to 6:30 is 30 minutes. 35 + 30 = 1 hour 5 minutes.

items.q: How many months are there in 5 years?
items.e: 1 year = 12 months: 5 × 12 = 60 months.

items.q: How many months are there in 9 years?
items.e: 1 year = 12 months: 9 × 12 = 108 months.

items.q: How many days are there in 4 weeks?
items.e: 1 week = 7 days: 4 × 7 = 28 days.

items.q: How many days are there in October (not a leap year)?
items.e: Thirty days have September, April, June and November; February has 28 (29 in a leap year); the rest have 31: 31.

items.q: How many months are there in 8 years?
items.e: 1 year = 12 months: 8 × 12 = 96 months.

items.q: How many days are there in May (not a leap year)?
items.e: Thirty days have September, April, June and November; February has 28 (29 in a leap year); the rest have 31: 31.

items.q: How many days are there in 3 weeks?
items.e: 1 week = 7 days: 3 × 7 = 21 days.

items.q: How many months are there in 6 years?
items.e: 1 year = 12 months: 6 × 12 = 72 months.

items.q: Today is Wednesday. What day of the week will it be in 19 days?
items.e: 19 days = 2 weeks and 5 days. Count on 5 days from Wednesday: Monday.

items.q: Today is Wednesday. What day of the week will it be in 15 days?
items.e: 15 days = 2 weeks and 1 day. Count on 1 day from Wednesday: Thursday.

items.q: Today is Tuesday. What day of the week will it be in 3 days?
items.e: 3 days = 0 weeks and 3 days. Count on 3 days from Tuesday: Friday.

items.q: Today is Saturday. What day of the week will it be in 17 days?
items.e: 17 days = 2 weeks and 3 days. Count on 3 days from Saturday: Tuesday.

items.q: Today is Sunday. What day of the week will it be in 17 days?
items.e: 17 days = 2 weeks and 3 days. Count on 3 days from Sunday: Wednesday.

items.q: Today is Saturday. What day of the week will it be in 29 days?
items.e: 29 days = 4 weeks and 1 day. Count on 1 day from Saturday: Sunday.

items.q: A holiday starts on 16 January and ends on 6 February. How many days is that, counting both the first and the last day?
items.e: January has 31 days: 31 − 16 = 15 days left in January, plus 6 days in February, plus the first day: 22 days.

items.q: A holiday starts on 13 June and ends on 1 July. How many days is that, counting both the first and the last day?
items.e: June has 30 days: 30 − 13 = 17 days left in June, plus 1 day in July, plus the first day: 19 days.

items.q: A holiday starts on 24 March and ends on 8 April. How many days is that, counting both the first and the last day?
items.e: March has 31 days: 31 − 24 = 7 days left in March, plus 8 days in April, plus the first day: 16 days.

items.q: A holiday starts on 2 June and ends on 24 July. How many days is that, counting both the first and the last day?
items.e: June has 30 days: 30 − 2 = 28 days left in June, plus 24 days in July, plus the first day: 53 days.

items.q: A holiday starts on 21 June and ends on 14 July. How many days is that, counting both the first and the last day?
items.e: June has 30 days: 30 − 21 = 9 days left in June, plus 14 days in July, plus the first day: 24 days.

items.q: A holiday starts on 6 February and ends on 16 March. How many days is that, counting both the first and the last day?
items.e: February has 28 days: 28 − 6 = 22 days left in February, plus 16 days in March, plus the first day: 39 days.

items.q: Joy starts reading at 7:08 p.m. and reads for 15 minutes. What time does Joy finish reading?
Ngozi starts football practice at 5:55 p.m. and practices for 1 hour 30 minutes. What time does Ngozi finish practice?
items.e: Add in two jumps. 5:55 p.m. + 5 minutes = 6:00 p.m. Then add the other 1 hour 25 minutes: 7:25 p.m.

items.q: Kayode puts a cake in the oven at 2:45 p.m. and bakes it for 15 minutes. What time does Kayode take the cake out?
Yusuf starts a movie at 6:28 p.m. and watches it for 40 minutes. What time does Yusuf finish the movie?
items.e: Add in two jumps. 6:28 p.m. + 32 minutes = 7:00 p.m. Then add the other 8 minutes: 7:08 p.m.

items.q: Chiamaka starts homework at 5:00 p.m. and works for 40 minutes. What time does Chiamaka finish homework?
Simi gets on the school bus at 7:00 a.m. and rides for 20 minutes. What time does Simi get to school?
Ngozi starts piano practice at 4:04 p.m. and plays for 45 minutes. What time does Ngozi stop playing?
Tolu starts cleaning the room at 10:25 a.m. and cleans for 1 hour 5 minutes. What time does Tolu finish cleaning?
items.e: Add in two jumps. 10:25 a.m. + 35 minutes = 11:00 a.m. Then add the other 30 minutes: 11:30 a.m.

items.q: Omar starts a bike ride at 10:05 a.m. and rides for 45 minutes. What time does Omar finish the ride?
Kelechi starts painting a picture at 3:16 p.m. and paints for 1 hour 30 minutes. What time does Kelechi finish painting?
items.e: Add in two jumps. 3:16 p.m. + 44 minutes = 4:00 p.m. Then add the other 46 minutes: 4:46 p.m.

items.q: Bisi finished a swim lesson at 4:40 p.m. It took 40 minutes. What time did it start?
items.e: Count back 40 minutes from 4:40 p.m.: 4:00 p.m.

items.q: Dayo finished a maths test at 4:05 p.m. It took 1 hour 10 minutes. What time did it start?
items.e: Count back in two jumps: 4:05 p.m. − 5 minutes = 4:00 p.m. Then go back the other 1 hour 5 minutes: 2:55 p.m.

items.q: Kayode finished a game at 6:30 p.m. It took 40 minutes. What time did it start?
items.e: Count back in two jumps: 6:30 p.m. − 30 minutes = 6:00 p.m. Then go back the other 10 minutes: 5:50 p.m.

items.q: Victor finished a walk at 6:05 p.m. It took 50 minutes. What time did it start?
items.e: Count back in two jumps: 6:05 p.m. − 5 minutes = 6:00 p.m. Then go back the other 45 minutes: 5:15 p.m.

items.q: Tunde finished a show at 6:20 p.m. It took 50 minutes. What time did it start?
items.e: Count back in two jumps: 6:20 p.m. − 20 minutes = 6:00 p.m. Then go back the other 30 minutes: 5:30 p.m.

items.q: Uju finished a class trip at 7:05 p.m. It took 55 minutes. What time did it start?
items.e: Count back in two jumps: 7:05 p.m. − 5 minutes = 7:00 p.m. Then go back the other 50 minutes: 6:10 p.m.

items.q: Joy got to the park at 1:40 p.m. and left at 2:35 p.m. How long was Joy there?
items.e: Jump to the next hour first: 1:40 to 2:00 is 20 minutes. Then 2:00 to 2:35 is 35 minutes. 20 + 35 = 55 minutes.

items.q: Ngozi got to the library at 9:40 p.m. and left at 10:05 p.m. How long was Ngozi there?
items.e: Jump to the next hour first: 9:40 to 10:00 is 20 minutes. Then 10:00 to 10:05 is 5 minutes. 20 + 5 = 25 minutes.

items.q: Kayode got to the museum at 8:55 p.m. and left at 9:40 p.m. How long was Kayode there?
items.e: Jump to the next hour first: 8:55 to 9:00 is 5 minutes. Then 9:00 to 9:40 is 40 minutes. 5 + 40 = 45 minutes.

items.q: Yusuf got to swim practice at 9:10 p.m. and left at 9:55 p.m. How long was Yusuf there?
items.e: Count on from 9:10 to 9:55: 55 − 10 = 45 minutes.
